A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction benchmarks, architectural ablations, timing measurements, spatial-cognition results and point-map evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds ScanNet++ evaluation, pruning analysis, register-token ablation and camera-pose robustness experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds a rendering-time pruning variant that discards Gaussians with target-view opacity below 0.01 (Section 5). The core architecture, training objectives and prediction procedure remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that pruning replaces the procedure used for existing benchmarks.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot ScanNet++ reconstruction with 16, 32 and 64 input views, plus DL3DV reconstruction under noisy camera poses. Existing datasets and tasks, including appendix spatial cognition and point-map estimation, are retained.

E2.justification: Table 16 adds an explicit theoretical FLOPs comparison against global-attention and alternating-attention variants. Empirical comparator membership in retained benchmarks is unchanged; the new ScanNet++ benchmark reuses Long-LRM and iLRM.

E3.justification: New protocols cover pose perturbations at 32 views and 960×540, register removal with feature-norm measurements, and per-image rendering after pruning. Existing training and evaluation settings are retained. Appendix A corrects 196 input views to 192, matching both versions' tables; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence beyond the retained hierarchy, feature-fusion and group-size ablations. New studies examine pruning trade-offs, register-token effects and controlled rotation/translation perturbations (Tables 7, 14 and 17), addressing rendering redundancy, feature stability and dependence on accurate poses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The standard deviations introduced in Table 17 specify injected pose noise, not uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for ScanNet++, pruning, register tokens, theoretical FLOPs and noisy poses. Table 17 reports PSNR falling from 25.96 to 20.85 under translation noise of standard deviation 0.005. Among retained quantitative tables, Table 2 changes MVP's 256-view LPIPS from 0.128 to 0.125; other entries match. v1 Figure 4's individual RE10K example is removed.

T1.justification: Table 16 introduces symbolic FLOPs expressions for global attention, alternating attention and MVP under stated layer and tokenizer assumptions. This is a limited analytical addition; the original method equations remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: dual hierarchical attention, scalable feed-forward reconstruction and a favorable quality–efficiency trade-off. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies sensitivity to inaccurate camera poses, especially translation errors, and discusses calibrated-camera applications and future pose-free extensions. It also connects register-token benefits to reduced feature norms. v1's detailed temporal-modeling and geometry-supervision future-work discussion is condensed.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the 0.01 pruning threshold, specifies RTX 4090 hardware and single-image timing for the rendering analysis, and states that the register ablation reuses the main ablation configuration. Core implementation details, training schedules, software choices and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds ScanNet++ and Depth Anything 3 references and positions MVP as a foundation for future pose-free extensions. It removes the dynamic-view-synthesis and 4D Gaussian Splatting citations associated with the shortened conclusion. The principal related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, shortens implementation prose and the conclusion, adds acknowledgements and author-contribution footnotes, and inserts analysis paragraphs. The overall section structure and most existing exposition are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a compact architecture schematic, ScanNet++ images and tables for the new analyses. It removes the main-text RE10K example while retaining the appendix RE10K illustrations. Other figures largely retain their content, with renumbering, table relocation and local layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The pruning, register-token and pose-noise studies provide useful evidence about efficiency, design choices and applicability, while ScanNet++ adds external-dataset validation. These improve assessment of the retained method. The gain is limited by an inconsistency in the new FLOPs table: Table 16's MVP expression evaluates to approximately 0.122 PFLOPs for its largest listed input, whereas the numerical entry is 0.81.
